1.title: Merging and Resolving Conflicts
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Merging and Resolving Conflicts. It covers the exam area Part two: Branching and history. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Merge with a fast-forward or a merge commit. Explain the three-way merge. Use --no F F and --F F only. Read conflict markers and the status of unmerged paths. Resolve a conflict and finish with git commit or git merge --continue. Abort with git merge --abort. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Two kinds of merge
1.text: Two kinds of merge. git merge branch brings the commits of another branch into the branch you are on, so you stand on the branch that receives the work. The result is one of two shapes, shown in the figure.

1.title: Two kinds of merge, continued
1.text: Two kinds of merge. The figure shows this: Two merge results: a fast-forward only moves the main pointer along a straight line, while a merge commit joins two lines of history with a commit that has two parents.

1.title: Two kinds of merge, continued
1.text: Two kinds of merge. When. Fast-forward: The current branch has no new commits. Merge commit: Both branches have new commits. What Git does. Fast-forward: Moves the pointer forward. Merge commit: Creates a new commit. Parents of the result. Fast-forward: One. Merge commit: Two. History. Fast-forward: A straight line. Merge commit: Shows the side branch. Two options control the choice. the no ff flag forces a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible, which keeps the branch visible in history. the ff only flag allows only a fast-forward and stops with an error when the branches have diverged.

1.title: Two kinds of merge, continued
1.text: Two kinds of merge. When both sides have new commits, Git does a three-way merge. It finds the merge base, the latest commit both branches share ( git merge base ), compares each tip with that base and combines the two sets of changes. If they touch different places, Git merges them on its own. Your hashes will differ from the ones in this module.

1.title: Two kinds of merge, continued
1.text: Two kinds of merge. A merge commit has two parents. The first is the branch you were on and the second is the branch you merged. git rev list the parents flag dash n one head prints the commit and its parents, so three hashes mean a merge commit. In the next block, main has a new commit that feature or banner lacks, so the branches have diverged.

1.title: A conflict and how to read it
1.text: A conflict and how to read it. A conflict happens when both branches changed the same lines of a file. Git merges everything it can, stops, and marks the file. Here main changed the shipping line of cart.txt to seven and feature or shipping changed it to free. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: A conflict and how to read it, continued
1.text: A conflict and how to read it. git status says You have unmerged paths and lists the file as both modified. U U is the short form. The last command lists only the unmerged files, which helps in a big merge. While paths are unmerged, git commit is refused. A merge in progress is recorded in dot git slash merge head. Git writes conflict markers into the file. Lines outside the markers merged cleanly.

1.title: A conflict and how to read it, continued
1.text: A conflict and how to read it. head. Start: the lines below are from the branch you are on. Divider between the two versions. feature slash shipping. End: the lines above are from the merged branch.

1.title: Resolve, continue or abort
1.text: Resolve, continue or abort. To resolve a conflict, edit the file to the content you want and delete the three marker lines. You may keep one side, the other, or write something new that combines both. Then run git add file to mark it resolved. git status now says all conflicts are fixed but you are still merging. Finish with git commit, which proposes the message "Merge branch 'feature or shipping'", or with git merge the continue flag. Both create the merge commit.

1.title: Resolve, continue or abort, continued
1.text: Resolve, continue or abort. If you are unsure, abort. git merge the abort flag returns the branch to the state before the merge: a clean tree, no markers, and no dot git slash merge head. To take one whole side, use the ours flag or the theirs flag, then git add the file.

2.title: Resolve, continue or abort, continued
2.text: Resolve, continue or abort. git checkout the ours flag file. The version from the branch you are on. git checkout the theirs flag file. The version from the branch you merge in. git checkout the merge flag file. Recreates the markers if you made a mess. git restore the ours flag file and the theirs flag do the same. In a merge, ours is the branch you stand on; in a ree base the meaning flips (module five). Two tools are worth knowing. git mergetool opens a visual merge tool that you have configured. git rerere records how you resolved a conflict and reuses it when the same conflict appears again. Tip: When a merge goes wrong, run git merge the abort flag and start again. It is safe before you commit, and it costs nothing.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. main has no new commits since Ada created feature or search and added two commits. She runs git merge feature slash search on main. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Git moves main forward to the tip of the branch. The branch has not diverged, so Git fast-forwards the main pointer and creates no new commit.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Both main and feature or banner have new commits. Bob runs git merge the ff only flag feature slash banner. What is the result? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Git stops with a fatal message and changes nothing. the ff only flag accepts only a fast-forward, so on diverged branches it refuses and leaves everything as it was.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. During a merge, git status dash s prints U U cart dot txt. What does it mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Both sides changed the file and the changes clash. U U marks an unmerged path where both sides modified the same lines.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. On main, Cy sees head, shipping seven,, shipping free, feature slash shipping. Which line came from main? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: shipping seven, because it sits under the head marker. Lines between the first marker and the divider are from the branch you are on.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Ada is merging feature or shipping into main and wants the whole cart.txt from feature or shipping. Which command takes it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: git checkout the theirs flag cart dot txt, then add the file. In a merge, theirs is the branch being merged in, and the file must be added afterwards to mark it resolved.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Bob started a merge and sees conflicts in many files. He wants the repository back as it was before the merge. What should he run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git merge the abort flag, which restores the earlier state. git merge the abort flag returns to the state before the merge started.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many parents does a merge commit have? Answer: Two. Question two. Which flag forces a merge commit when a fast-forward is possible? Answer: the no ff flag. Question three. Which command lists only the unmerged files? Answer: git diff the name only flag the diff filter flag set to U.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which two commands can finish a resolved merge? Answer: git commit or git merge the continue flag. Question five. What do the lines between and show? Answer: The version from the branch being merged in. Question six. What does git rerere do? Answer: It records a conflict resolution and reuses it when the same conflict appears again.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Fast-forward: Pointer moves, no new commit, one parent. Merge commit: Two parents; the no ff flag forces it; git rev list the parents flag dash n one head shows them. --F F only: Fails with "Not possible to fast-forward" when branches diverged. Three-way merge: Merge base plus the two tips; same lines changed means a conflict. Conflict status: Unmerged paths, both modified, U U; git diff the name only flag the diff filter flag set to U. Markers: head ours,, branch theirs. Resolve: Edit, git add, then git commit or git merge the continue flag. Abort: git merge the abort flag restores the state before the merge. Take a side: git checkout the ours flag or the theirs flag; git checkout the merge flag recreates markers.
